Enough is enough with Broadway jukebox musicals stitched together with threadbare and synthetic stories.

A jukebox musical that could undo all the genre rehab delivered by superior shows built around Carole King and, if you want to stretch the definition a bit to include Lazarus, David Bowie, Broadway‘s Summer: The Donna Summer Musical, opening tonight, is as unimaginative as its title.

Anyone who worked as hard for her money - and for a professional respect that came too late - as Donna Summer did deserves so much more than this.
